input:
You are knight_b1, one of sixteen agents playing White in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 19. the team planned Nc3 (knight_b1), but knight_b1 (amnesia) sent Ng3 instead, and that move was played, costing 10 centipawns.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 5. the team planned c4 (pawn_c2), but pawn_d2 (greed) sent dxc5 instead, and that move was played, costing 7 centipawns.
- On move 16. the team planned b4 (pawn_b2), but pawn_b2 (amnesia) sent b3 instead, and that move was played, costing 27 centipawns.

How your team coordinates: over a chat channel. Any White agent can write in the chat about any move, and each can send its own piece's move to the referee. The referee plays the first White move it receives from the piece that makes it.

Your team keeps a shared file, RULES.md. Any White agent can read it and write to it. Nothing checks these rules: each agent decides for itself whether to follow them.

RULES.md now:
- Only the piece named in the team's agreed plan may send a move this turn; every other agent stays silent on the move channel, even if it can capture something or feels threatened, and the planned piece sends exactly the agreed move and nothing else.
- Before sending any move, the planned piece must re-read the agreed plan in chat and confirm that the move it is about to send matches the plan's piece and destination square exactly, and every other agent must send no move at all, even to capture or escape a threat, unless the team has first agreed in chat to change the plan.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule to add to RULES.md that would help your team win.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>", "covers": [<the off-plan moves an agent who follows the rule would not send: any of "panic", "greed", "amnesia">]}
response: {"rule": "The planned piece must paste the plan's exact move (e.g. 'Nc3') into chat and copy that same string verbatim into its move command, and if the plan names a different piece than itself, it sends nothing.", "covers": ["amnesia", "greed", "panic"]}
